summary: Caddy is an open source web server designed to handle HTTP traffic with built-in, automated TLS certificate management. Written in Go, it can be run as a containerised service or installed via standard package managers like deb. It simplifies the setup and maintenance of web services by automating HTTPS configuration out of the box.
goodFor: It is a strong fit if you want a modern web server that manages TLS certificates automatically without complex external tooling like Certbot.
watchOut: Migrating complex routing and security rules from established alternatives like Nginx or Apache may require rewriting configuration syntax to match Caddy's structure.
deployNotes: You will typically run this via Docker or a deb package, ensuring persistent storage is mounted for your site files and certificate cache.
